# A test missing from this file is NOT skipped — it is assigned the mean
# of its own suite's rows, so the file going stale makes shards less even
# and never makes one incomplete. scripts/test-integration-shard.sh
# asserts completeness independently of this file, and
# scripts/check-durations-table.sh goes red the moment the rows stop
# naming exactly the tests the partitioner places.
# POPULATION: TOP-LEVEL TEST FUNCTIONS, PARENTS ONLY.
# One row per `func TestX(t *testing.T)` in test/integration/*_test.go —
# 95 of them, the main suite's 91 and the failure suite's 4. A subtest's
# seconds are inside its parent's figure and are NOT a row of their own.
# That is stated because the previous edition's header did not state it
# and the population was read back two ways: 104 rows summing 1804.88s
# (parents and subtests, a subtest counted twice) against 91 top-level
# rows. The extraction below excludes subtests by construction — the
# `--- PASS:` lines it reads are anchored at column zero and the name
# class carries no `/`, which is what a subtest's line has.
#   source     the three consecutive successful Integration runs of the
#              v6-wiring branch that produced suite logs for the tree
#              Earlier runs are deliberately NOT sampled: the v6 tests
#              they cost had different bodies, which is drift in the
#              subject rather than in the runner.
#   method     median of the per-test `--- PASS/SKIP/FAIL: <name> (<n>s)`
#              lines across the three runs. Median rather than mean: the
#              ephemeral runner pool produces occasional slow jobs and
#              one such sample should not move a test's weight.
#   one row     TestLeaseRenewIPv6_HonorsT1 is 73.85, and it alone is NOT
#              from the corpus runs above: this round changed that test's
#              body (its baseline moved from the bind to t1-t1Slop), so
#              the 90.03 the corpus measured costs a tree that no longer
#              exists — drift in the subject, which the note above says
#              is the one thing that disqualifies a sample. Its figure
#              is the median of the same test on the three head runs
#              73.85. Same method, three samples, a later corpus.
#   samples    3 for all 95. No row is inferred. The previous edition
#              carried four inferred rows and fourteen v6 rows recovered
#              from the 1.9.0 corpus; every one of those is now measured
#              against the client that actually ships here.
#   spread     min and max per test across the three samples are not
#              stored, but were read: the widest single-test spread was
#              and 90 of the 95 spread under 3s. A row is a median of
# THE SHARD COUNTS ARE DERIVED FROM THESE NUMBERS AND THE BUDGET (D41).
# The maintainer's bar is that everything on the way into the branch
# finishes well under five minutes. The measured window is the suite
# jobs' first start to the aggregate's verdict, so the arithmetic is
#   window = max over jobs(fixed + test seconds) + aggregate (8s measured)
# `fixed` is what a suite job costs before and after the tests. Since
# D41 the plugin is built ONCE per run and installed from an artifact,
# so `fixed` no longer carries a build: MEASURED at the base it was 13s
# of job setup, checkout and post-steps plus 82-90s of `make plugin`
# plus 28s of `go test` compilation and the harness package; the build
# term is gone and the download and install replace it.
# Packing the medians above with the same greedy longest-first packer
#           OF=2   154.6s   <- ships; the floor is one test,
# Nine and two. Nine is where the main suite's longest shard first lands
# far enough under the budget that a fixed cost of ~60s and an ephemeral
# pool's job-to-job variance both fit inside it; the failure suite is
# split at its own floor, which no further shard can improve because one
# test is 155s of a real lease lapsing.
# where six shipped before: that is the price, and it is paid in pool
# capacity (16 runners, MEASURED from the runners API 2026-09-08), not
# in wall clock. Past nine each extra main shard buys ~20s for a whole
# runner slot and the failure suite becomes the critical path at OF=12.
# REFRESH RECIPE. Take the three most recent consecutive successful
